label: early original-phase steps after a leading v (v at position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase at steps 2-4 when the sequence starts with v (first token v), or at steps 3-4 when v is the second token. It is token-independent at the current step: the input there can be any letter or digit. Activation peaks at t=3 (51% of mass) and is strongest when the sequence opens with v v (top examples are v v v... and v v h...). It falls off by t=5 and is essentially zero at t=0-1, at the delimiter (0.7% of mass), and in the copy phase. A v appearing later in the sequence does not trigger it (seen(v) alone has precision 0.53). Weak residual activations show up on non-v sequences around t=3.

issues: Minor: the t=4 cells are less clean than t=2-3. orig(0)==v at t=4 has precision 0.82 and orig(1)==v at t=4 has 0.75, so most of the false positives sit at t=4 where the activation is fading. The t=2 and t=3 cells for orig(0)==v both have precision 1.0, and orig(1)==v at t=3 has 0.86.

Minor tail: when v is at position 2, the feature sometimes fires at t=4 (precision 0.26, recall 4.6%, mass 2.6%). This is a weak continuation of the same pattern. Adding it would hurt precision, so it is not a systematic gap worth adding to the predicate.

Checks that held: mass by t is 0.257 / 0.513 / 0.211 for t=2/3/4. Delimiter mass is 0.007 and copy-phase mass is 0.000. t=0-1 has zero activations. Sequences with no v at position 0 or 1 at t=3 have precision 0.006 and only show up in the lowest activation quartile, matching the claim of weak leftovers. v v openings have precision 1.0 and are overrepresented in mass. orig(1)==v at t=2 is correctly excluded (precision 0.036). The cells at t=5 are each under 2% of mass.

Test misses are scattered (3.3% of mass, all low magnitude). Test false positives are mostly t=4 steps where the feature has faded. Test scores reproduce: precision 0.893, recall 0.880, F1 0.887, mass recall 0.967.
